selection: Six distinct mineral species and one spent-electrolyte resource extend the corpus. Autunite and torbernite retain qualified synthetic-crystal identity evidence. Inyoite and szaibelyite retain abiotic pressure/thermal observations; rhabdophane-(Ce) and rhabdophane-(La) retain separate hydrothermal/thermal transformations. Spent vanadium flow-battery electrolyte combines two clearly separated abiotic recovery and regeneration studies. Mineral species, elemental materials, fresh electrolyte and used secondary resources remain distinct. No microbial process or elemental criticality is inherited.

source_issues.body:
Comboni et al. (2022), [DOI 10.1007/s00269-021-01173-3](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00269-021-01173-3), was inspected as the complete institutional Revision_1 accepted manuscript with publisher-linked Table S1 and twelve CIFs. The version-of-record PDF was not acquired.

The abstract gives a maximum 19.80(5) GPa, whereas Table 1 ends at 18.91(5) GPa and body text uses 18.9 GPa. At 2.00(5) GPa, Table 1 gives 944.0(1) cubic angstroms while the corresponding CIF gives 923.96(11). A pressure comment in deposited file 10 also needs reconciliation with its run metadata. The current inyoite owner retains the first two conflicts, restricts deposits to the low-pressure polymorph and does not claim a solved or recovered inyoite-II structure.

Acceptance: obtain the legitimate final text, corrected run table or authoritative clarification; map each CIF to pressure and volume without silently repairing values. Check the historical Mount Blanco/Death Valley versus Kramer attribution separately from the unreported locality of the experimental museum crystal. Preserve source versions and uncertainty; do not infer a reversible transition, phase yield or natural occurrence of inyoite-II.

Owner: data/records/inyoite.yaml. Full provenance and locators: research/sources/round103-borates/20261015T212242Z-source-investigation.json.

source_issues.body:
Marincea (2001), [DOI 10.2113/gscanmin.39.1.111](https://doi.org/10.2113/gscanmin.39.1.111), and the relevant sections of the [1998 thesis](https://theses.hal.science/tel-01027512v1/file/19980615-Marincea-S.pdf) share specimens/data and are not independent replication.

Article Methods specify nitrogen and 10 degrees C/min for the DSC arm; Table 7 footnote 2 specifies 20 degrees C/min. Thesis Table 30 repeats specimen rows but specifies argon and 20 degrees C/min. Vacuum conditioning at 20 degrees C for one hour and heating at 110 degrees C for twelve hours are not explicitly assigned to separate aliquots. Appendix Table A.22 uses 1402 BB where Table 32/article use 1406. The thesis temperature-resolved diffraction arm is Cacova Ierii specimen 1821; it must not become a Baita Bihor result.

Acceptance: acquire attributable instrument/aliquot records or authoritative correction to resolve atmosphere, ramp, pretreatment and specimen labels. Keep impurities, distinct localities, total versus main-event loss and source temperature ranges separate. Obtain the Grice 2008 diffraction deposit and earlier hydroxyl-ascharite comparison if available before extending those conclusions. Current data/records/szaibelyite.yaml explicitly preserves these limits; its provenance is in research/sources/round103-borates/20261015T212242Z-source-investigation.json.

Bamforth et al. (2024), [DOI 10.1016/j.chemgeo.2024.122307](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chemgeo.2024.122307), complete original and mmc1.xlsx, support the bounded abiotic conversion in data/records/rhabdophane-ce.yaml.

Section 2.1.2/page 4 says 20 +/- 0.1 mg per reactor, while Table 1 lists 20.9-21.1 mg for the nine fluids. Section 3.1/page 5 calls nominal-pH-3 replacement below 5%, but Figure 3 labels 4.4%, 4.7% and 6.4%. The record retains these contradictions. Its separate nominal-pH-1 comparison of 98.6% versus 6.4% is consistently reported and represents fitted crystalline phase proportions, not cerium recovery.

Acceptance: obtain corrected loading/phase-quantification records or legitimate source-level clarification; verify fluid, row and denominator mapping. Preserve the PXRD detection limit and distinction between proposed mechanism and direct measurements. source_issues.body:
Shelyug et al. (2018), [DOI 10.3389/fchem.2018.00604](https://doi.org/10.3389/fchem.2018.00604), complete original and supplementary Table_1.DOCX, has generalized trend wording that does not follow all reported quantities.

The abstract describes water decreasing as rare-earth ionic radius increases, while Table 2 gives La 0.804 and Gd 0.533 waters per phosphate. Page 4 groups dehydration and transition temperatures under an increasing-radius trend, while page 5/Figure 4 distinguish decreasing monazite-transformation temperatures. These processes and quantities require separate interpretation. Thermogravimetric total water includes adsorbed and structural contributions and is not a refined water-site occupancy.

Acceptance: verify any publisher correction or attributable clarification and reconcile the exact plotted quantities and uncertainties. Do not revise current IMA formulas from sample water loss. The Ce/La owners retain sample-specific water and bounded thermal conversion, excluding the contradictory generalizations. Dossier: research/sources/round103-ree-phosphates/20261015T212204Z-source-investigation.json.

source_issues.body:
Yang and Wang (2016), [DOI 10.16085/j.issn.1000-6613.2016.09.047](https://doi.org/10.16085/j.issn.1000-6613.2016.09.047), complete five-page publisher original, reports a one-cubic-metre pilot treatment of supplied failed positive electrolyte and an ammonium-metavanadate product. This is separate from later laboratory-aged electrolyte regeneration.

The conclusion gives pH 2.0-2.5 whereas Methods, results and abstract use 8.0-8.5. Method and summary time ranges differ; Table 4 reaches its reported 99.01% concentration-based precipitation metric at 120/140 minutes, not the separate 80-minute endpoint. Figure 2 and residual assay labels use V2O5 equivalents despite generic vanadium wording. The 148.30 kg powder and reported 99.58% dry-basis assay do not establish an independently verified overall vanadium balance or continuous industrial deployment. No product diffraction pattern or explicit NH4VO3 assay procedure is supplied in the inspected original.

Acceptance: acquire an attributable correction or original run/assay documentation resolving pH, time and concentration basis; establish initial/intermediate/final volumes and phase inventories before adding overall recovery. Obtain product characterization, assay methods, replication and uncertainty before strengthening purity/yield claims. Owner: data/records/spent-vanadium-flow-battery-electrolyte.yaml. Dossier: research/sources/round103-electrolyte/20261015T211843Z-source-investigation.json.

source_issues.body:
Peng et al. (2024), [DOI 10.7513/j.issn.1004-7638.2024.03.002](https://doi.org/10.7513/j.issn.1004-7638.2024.03.002), complete seven-page publisher original, uses purchased electrolyte aged in a laboratory cell until capacity fell below half the rated value. It does not establish performance for returned commercial waste.

Results assign 93% capacity recovery to direct electrolysis and 92% to acid electrolysis; abstract/conclusion reverse them. The asymmetric section also misnames the acid arm for a 92% value. The stated 1190 mAh target conflicts with 2238 mA for 30 minutes, which calculates to 1119 mAh. The current owner preserves both discrepancies without inventing corrected figures.

Acceptance: obtain original arm-labelled cycling/current/time data or authoritative correction; distinguish capacity restoration, coulombic efficiency and recovered-metal yield. Account for discarded/transferred compartments and the acid arm's replaced graphite felt/collector. Verify aging duration, temperature, flow, replicates and uncertainty before broader comparison. Short sequential cycles are not independent replicates or deployment evidence. Owner: data/records/spent-vanadium-flow-battery-electrolyte.yaml. Dossier: research/sources/round103-electrolyte/20261015T211843Z-source-investigation.json.
